title: Cold rebuild: diagnose four stopped containers
summary: Find why four containers stopped and fix one, on a real Docker Engine, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *debugging crashing containers* you found why four real containers stopped and
brought one back. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks
are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: **"The container exits immediately."** `docker ps -a` shows `Exited (0) 1 second ago`. The Dockerfile ends with `CMD service nginx start`. What is wrong?
options: `service nginx start` launches nginx as a background daemon and returns; PID 1 ends, so the container ends. Run nginx in the foreground: `CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]`
Exit code 0 means Docker killed it for using too much memory
steps.explain: A container lives as long as its main process. Servers must stay in the foreground.

steps.title: Diagnose four stopped containers, cold
prompt: A real Docker Engine runs in this terminal. Four containers stopped: `cache`, `web`, `worker` and `api`.
1. Write one line per container into `~/answers/diagnosis.txt`, `NAME CAUSE`, with CAUSE one of `oom`, `finished`,
2. Run `web` again (same name, image `shop/web:1.0`) so that it stays up.
From memory: no hints this time.
